_comment: RED baseline (RLOO variant), second attempt: identical to red250.json except the advantage rule, which is R4. red250.json is kept unchanged as the record of what produced runs/red250. R4 is A_{i,t} = A_seq_i + red_alpha * (r^final_{i,t} - mean_t r^final_{i,t}), with A_seq_i RLOO's own leave-one-out advantage -- the sequence contrast carries the level and RED's redistribution only decides which tokens within a response receive it. R3, the first rule, subtracted the sequence-scale baseline b_i off every token instead; on a group whose rewards are all negative that made every token's advantage positive, the update stopped being contrastive, and runs/red250 collapsed to degenerate 2-token responses from rollout 50 and then crashed at 68. See red/RED_REPRO_NOTES.md 2.2 for the measurements and the retirement. Everything else is still copied from formal250.json so this arm stays comparable with GRPO, VPO-RM and P2T; only the credit assignment differs. Paper-specific notes: (1) beta_c is RED Eq. (7)'s convex-combination weight, 1.0 removes the sparse sequence term entirely; (2) the KL coefficient rides in 'beta' and is applied INSIDE the reward per Eq. (8), so the trainer applies no separate KL loss term; (3) clip_eps and advantage_std_floor_fraction are carried for config parity. advantage_std_floor_fraction is genuinely unread by a RED update (RED does not standardise the advantage), but clip_eps IS read in three places that do not clip the objective: the validation below, the rollout_direct_ratio_clip_fraction metric, and the startup gate on trainer-vs-sampler agreement. Do not set it to 0 or 1 to mean 'no clipping' -- that fails validation. The run manifest stamps red_clipping, red_advantage_rule and red_alpha so the actual behaviour is never ambiguous after the fact. TABLE 7 DEVIATIONS are kept deliberately, not overlooked: beta is 0.03 against the paper's 0.02, group_size is 8 against RLOO sample K 4, max_response_tokens is 2048 against 1024/688/512, and the harmfulness/helpfulness two-model setup of the paper's SafeRLHF experiments is not implemented. Aligning any of those would break comparability with this project's other arms, so they stay recorded as deviations in RED_REPRO_NOTES.md section 1. DEVICE PLAN: three cards, one per role. actor_device/reward_device are ABSOLUTE ids (4 and 5) and vllm_gpus must be the single physical card generation should own (vllm.py hands that list to the subprocess as its own CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, and tp=1 takes the first entry). Launch WITHOUT RED_GPUS so CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES stays unset; binding via a remapped list instead would trip the trainer's device-plan check, which requires the visible list to be 0..n-1. GPUs 0-3 are free now that p2t250 has finished, so moving this arm onto them would restore that check -- untested here, and 4/5/6 is the path both smoke runs exercised. push_every is 5: the owner approved autopush, knowing commits land on the local p2t-baseline branch and are pushed to p2t-origin/main, and that autopush stages the whole tree (git add -A). checkpoint_interval and keep_checkpoints stay at the sibling's 20/2 even though red250's two surviving checkpoints were both already past its collapse and its last healthy state was never recoverable: tests/red/test_trainer.py pins every shared training parameter against formal250.json, and this arm's whole purpose is to differ from its siblings in the credit assignment and nothing else. The protection against a repeat is the health gate instead. Launch the watcher with stop-on-problem so a collapse costs the rollouts it took to detect rather than the whole budget: bash red/scripts/watch_red.sh red250b 30 stop-on-problem. With a 20-rollout checkpoint interval that can still cost up to 20 rollouts of recoverable progress when it fires, which is the accepted trade for not diverging from the sibling's cadence; change both numbers here and in the sibling arm's config together if that trade is ever revisited
